nodes.name: Modified Sol-Gel Synthesis
nodes.procedure: SnCl₂ (Aldrich, 99.99%) and Sb₂O₃ (Aldrich, 99.99%) were first dissolved in a 0.1 M HNO₃ aqueous solution. After the two solutions were mixed, NH₄OH solution (Aldrich) was used as a pH regulator (pH ∼ 5). Chelation of the metal cations was then achieved by adding citric acid to the aqueous solution in a 2:1 ratio with respect to the total metal cations. Ethylene glycol was added in the last step to polymerize the organic precursor. The solution was heated under stirring and once the gel was obtained, it was washed and then dried at 150 °C overnight.

nodes.procedure: The powder precursor was calcined in O₂ at 550 °C for 2 h with a heating/cooling rate of 5 °C min⁻¹. Based on TGA results showing main weight loss up to 550°C.

nodes.name: Pt Deposition on Optimized Support
nodes.procedure: Pt/Sb-SnO₂ electrodes were prepared depositing Pt nanoparticles on the Sb-SnO₂ porous thin films (optimized, calcined 2h) by DC magnetron sputtering. Pt deposition parameters optimized to obtain 10 μg cm⁻² Pt loading with primary particle size 2-3 nm.

nodes.description: Accelerated stability test for Sb-SnO2 support
nodes.source_text: For the sample calcined for 10 h a strong modification of the CV was observed, going towards a reduction of ∼12% of both anodic and cathodic charges.

nodes.description: Electrochemical stability test under PEFC cathode conditions
nodes.source_text: To test the electrochemical stability of Pt/Sb-SnO2 catalysts... CV measurements were performed over 1000 potential cycles between 0.5 and 1.5 V (RHE) using a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹... After the stability test the ORR activity for the Pt/Sb-SnO2 catalyst decreased by 26±10%.
After the electrochemical stability test, the ORR activity of the Pt/AB catalysts decreases by 65±7%.

nodes.description: Oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and selectivity
nodes.source_text: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity... was measured... using the thin-film rotating ring disk electrode (RRDE) technique... in O2-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 by cathodically scanning... at 5 mV s⁻¹... The activity... was 0.155±0.022 mA cm⁻²... mass activity of 15.5±2.2 mA mgPt⁻¹... H2O2 production reached up to 13%... 4-electron transfer process.
The ORR kinetic current at 0.9 V (RHE) for the Pt/AB pristine catalysts was 0.125±0.019 mA cm⁻², which corresponds to a mass activity of 12.5±1.9 mA mgpt⁻¹.

nodes.description: Electrochemical stability test of carbon support
nodes.source_text: Fig. 4c illustrates the CVs of acetylene black carbon before and after the same electrochemical stability test. As expected, a strong oxidation current at the highest potential was observed... Upon cycling the anodic current strongly decreased and growth of the quinone/hydroquinone redox couple around 0.55–0.7 V (RHE) was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA of powder precursor shows ~75% weight loss between 130-550°C due to organic matrix decomposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main weight loss (~75%) occurred between 130 and 550 °C due to the decomposition of the organic matrix.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows single phase rutile structure; crystallite size increases from 6±1 nm (2h) to 35±2 nm (10h calcination).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b shows the XRD patterns of Sb-SnO2 powders after calcination at 550 °C for 2 and 10 h. Both calcination processes led to single phase materials with a rutile structure... crystallite size, calculated using the Scherrer equation, increased from 6±1 to 35±2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area decreases from 53±8 m²/g (2h, 500°C) to 18±5 m²/g (10h calcination).
nodes.evidence_snippet: for the powder calcined at 500 °C for 2 h the BET surface area was 53±8 m² g⁻¹, while for the sample calcined for 10 h... 18±5 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of highest surface area powder shows primary particles 10-20 nm forming agglomerates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: primary particle size is in the range of 10-20 nm, with the primary particles forming larger agglomerates.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX bulk Sb content: 8.5±0.5 at% (2h), 8.3±0.6 at% (10h); after stability test 8.4±0.95 at% (2h), 0.8±0.6 at% (10h).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX showed... bulk Sb content, which resulted in slightly higher values than the projected value (5 at%).

nodes.evidence_snippet: the resistivity was evaluated to be 50±10 Ω cm and 2700±60 Ω cm for the sample calcined at 550 °C for 2 and 10 h, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV (1000 cycles 0.05-1.6 V, 50 mV/s) shows Sb5+/Sb3+ redox at 0.9-0.6 V RHE; 2h sample shows 7%/4.5% charge decrease vs ~12% for 10h sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a fairly visible redox couple at about 0.9-0.6 V (RHE) could be observed. The redox couple can be associated with reduction–oxidation of Sb ions between 5+ and 3+ oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: RRDE shows 4-electron ORR process on Pt/Sb-SnO2 with H2O2 yield 13% at 50 mV RHE decreasing to 7% at 0.1 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the lowest measured potential (50 mV RHE) the H2O2 production reached up to 13%, while it progressively decreased to 7% at 0.1 V (RHE) and went to almost zero at potential higher than ~0.6 V (RHE).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows increased particle size and agglomerates with longer annealing time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed that increasing the annealing time not only increased the average particle size but also the amount and the size of particle agglomerates.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV stability test of Pt/Sb-SnO2 (1000 cycles 0.5-1.5 V, 50 mV/s) shows Pt-oxide reduction peak shift to higher potential indicating Pt particle growth/agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The most noticeable change in the cyclic voltammograms upon cycling is related to the shift of the Pt-oxide reduction peak (~0.7 V RHE) towards a higher potential.
